<reason>B won by dismantling the mechanisms connecting market prices to better policy decisions. A offered a plausible case for dispersed information and incentivized dissent, but never resolved B’s objections about conditional forecasts confounding policy effects with policy selection, or traders accepting losses to purchase influence. B also showed that A’s promised accountability depended on the documentation rules A dismissed as paperwork. A defended an additional forecasting signal more successfully than the proposed shift in institutional reliance. B answered pressure more directly and made the comparative choice clearer.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s closing directly defeated A’s claim that money moving a price cannot be ignored: trading losses discipline traders, not officials, and making officials respond still requires governance rules. This exposed the central gap in A’s claimed self-enforcing accountability.</best_rebuttal>
